# THE LOEB CLASSICAL LIBRARY

**AESCHINES.** <note>An Athenian statesman and one of the ten Attic orators, known for his rivalry with Demosthenes.</note> C. D. Adams. (*2nd Impression*)
**AESCHYLUS.** <note>The earliest of the three great Greek tragedians whose plays have survived; he is often called the father of tragedy.</note> H. Weir Smyth. 2 Vols. (Vol. I *5th Impression*, Vol. II *4th Impression*)
**ALCIPHRON, AELIAN AND PHILOSTRATUS: LETTERS.** <note>A collection of fictional and historical letters from the later periods of Greek literature, offering a glimpse into social life and rhetoric.</note> A. R. Benner and F. H. Fobes.
**APOLLODORUS.** <note>A comprehensive handbook of Greek mythology and heroic legends, traditionally attributed to Apollodorus of Athens.</note> Sir James G. Frazer. 2 Vols. (*2nd Impression*)
**APOLLONIUS RHODIUS.** <note>Author of the "Argonautica," the epic poem detailing Jason and the Argonauts' quest for the Golden Fleece.</note> R. C. Seaton. (*4th Impression*)
**THE APOSTOLIC FATHERS.** <note>A collection of the earliest Christian writings outside the New Testament, written by authors who were believed to have personally known the Apostles.</note> Kirsopp Lake. 2 Vols. (*7th Impression*)
**APPIAN’S ROMAN HISTORY.** <note>An account of Rome's history written by a Greek historian, organized by the various peoples and regions the Romans conquered.</note> Horace White. 4 Vols. (Vol. I *3rd Impression*, Vols. II, III and IV *2nd Impression*)
**ARATUS.** <note>A didactic poet whose work "Phaenomena" describes the constellations and celestial phenomena.</note> *Compare* <note>original: "Cf."</note> **CALLIMACHUS.**

**ARISTOTLE: ART OF RHETORIC.** <note>A foundational treatise on the art of persuasion.</note> J. H. Freese. (*3rd Impression*)
**ARISTOTLE: ATHENIAN CONSTITUTION, EUDEMIAN ETHICS, VIRTUES AND VICES.** H. Rackham. (*3rd Impression*)
**ARISTOTLE: GENERATION OF ANIMALS.** <note>One of Aristotle's primary biological works, focusing on how animals reproduce.</note> A. L. Peck. (*2nd Impression*)
**ARISTOTLE: METAPHYSICS.** <note>A core work of philosophy dealing with the fundamental nature of reality and existence.</note> H. Tredennick. 2 Vols. (*3rd Impression*)
**ARISTOTLE: MINOR WORKS.** W. S. Hett. “On Colours,” “On Things Heard,” “Physiognomics,” “On Plants,” “On Marvellous Things Heard,” “Mechanical Problems,” “On Indivisible Lines,” “Situations and Names of Winds,” “On Melissus, Xenophanes, and Gorgias.”
**ARISTOTLE: NICOMACHEAN ETHICS.** <note>Aristotle’s most famous work on ethics, arguing that the goal of human life is happiness achieved through virtue.</note> H. Rackham. (*5th Impression revised.*)
**ARISTOTLE: OECONOMICA AND MAGNA MORALIA.** <note>The first work deals with household management (economics), while the second is a treatise on ethics.</note> G. C. Armstrong. (With Metaphysics, Vol. II.) (*3rd Impression*)
**ARISTOTLE: ON THE HEAVENS.** <note>Aristotle’s astronomical treatise describing his cosmological model of the universe.</note> W. K. C. Guthrie. (*2nd Impression*)
**ARISTOTLE: ON THE SOUL, SHORT TREATISES ON NATURE, ON BREATH.** <note>original: "Parva Naturalia"; a collection of short works on natural physical phenomena common to soul and body, such as memory and sleep.</note> W. S. Hett. (*2nd Impression revised.*)
**ARISTOTLE: ORGANON.** <note>The title given to Aristotle's collected works on logic, which he viewed as the "instrument" of all scientific reasoning.</note> H. P. Cooke and H. Tredennick. 3 Vols. Vol. I. (*2nd Impression*)
**ARISTOTLE: PARTS OF ANIMALS.** A. L. Peck; **MOTION AND PROGRESSION OF ANIMALS.** E. S. Forster. (*2nd Impression*)
**ARISTOTLE: PHYSICS.** <note>A foundational work in Western science and philosophy regarding the study of nature, motion, and change.</note> Rev. P. Wicksteed and F. M. Cornford. 2 Vols. (*2nd Impression*)
**ARISTOTLE: POETICS** and **LONGINUS.** W. Hamilton Fyfe; **DEMETRIUS ON STYLE.** W. Rhys Roberts. (*4th Impression revised.*) <note>A volume collecting essential Greek works on literary criticism, aesthetics, and the art of writing.</note>

**ARISTOTLE: PROBLEMS.** <note>A collection of questions and answers regarding various scientific and everyday phenomena, likely compiled by Aristotle's followers.</note> W. S. Hett. 2 Volumes. (Volume I **2nd Impression revised.**)
**ARISTOTLE: RHETORIC TO ALEXANDER.** <note>original: "RHETORICA AD ALEXANDRUM"; a manual of public speaking traditionally attributed to Aristotle, though likely written by Anaximenes of Lampsacus.</note> H. Rackham. (With Problems, Volume II.)
**ARRIAN: HISTORY OF ALEXANDER AND INDIAN HISTORY.** <note>original: "INDICA"; Arrian was a 2nd-century historian whose account of Alexander the Great's campaigns is considered the most reliable surviving source.</note> Reverend E. Iliffe Robson. 2 Volumes. (**2nd Impression**)
**ATHENAEUS: THE BANQUET OF THE LEARNED.** <note>original: "DEIPNOSOPHISTAE"; an immense work presenting a series of fictional conversations between scholars at a banquet, preserving thousands of fragments of lost Greek literature.</note> C. B. Gulick. 7 Volumes. (Volumes I, V and VI **2nd Impression**)
**ST. BASIL: LETTERS.** <note>A collection of correspondence by Basil of Caesarea, a leading 4th-century theologian and bishop who helped define early Christian orthodoxy.</note> R. J. Deferrari. 4 Volumes. (**2nd Impression**)
**CALLIMACHUS AND LYCOPHRON.** <note>Hellenistic poets known for their scholarly and often cryptic style.</note> A. W. Mair; **ARATUS.** <note>A poet whose work "Phaenomena" described the stars and weather signs.</note> G. R. Mair.
**CLEMENT OF ALEXANDRIA.** <note>A 2nd-century Christian philosopher who sought to harmonize Greek philosophy with Christian doctrine.</note> Reverend G. W. Butterworth. (**2nd Impression**)
**COLLUTHUS.** <note>A late Greek epic poet known for his work on the abduction of Helen.</note> Compare <note>original: "Cf."</note> **OPPIAN.**
**DAPHNIS AND CHLOE.** <note>The most famous of the ancient Greek pastoral romances.</note> Compare <note>original: "Cf."</note> **LONGUS.**
**DEMOSTHENES I: OLYNTHIACS, PHILIPPICS AND MINOR ORATIONS:** I-XVII and XX. <note>Demosthenes was the greatest of the Athenian orators; these speeches were famous for rousing resistance against Philip II of Macedon.</note> J. H. Vince.
**DEMOSTHENES II: ON THE CROWN AND ON THE FALSE EMBASSY.** <note>original: "DE CORONA AND DE FALSA LEGATIONE"; two of the most significant legal and political speeches of ancient Athens.</note> C. A. Vince and J. H. Vince. (**2nd Impression revised.**)
**DEMOSTHENES III: MEIDIAS, ANDROTION, ARISTOCRATES, TIMOCRATES, ARISTOGEITON.** <note>A collection of Demosthenes' legal speeches regarding public and political crimes.</note> J. H. Vince.
**DEMOSTHENES IV-VI: PRIVATE ORATIONS AND AGAINST NEAERA.** <note>original: "IN NEAERAM"; speeches concerning private lawsuits and the famous case against the woman Neaera regarding citizenship and marriage laws.</note> A. T. Murray. (Volume IV **2nd Impression**)
**DEMOSTHENES VII: FUNERAL SPEECH, EROTIC ESSAY, INTRODUCTIONS AND LETTERS.** <note>original: "EXORDIA"; a collection of miscellaneous works attributed to the orator.</note> N. W. and N. J. DeWitt.
**DIO CASSIUS: ROMAN HISTORY.** <note>A massive 80-volume history of Rome written in Greek by a high-ranking Roman official of Greek descent.</note> E. Cary. 9 Volumes. (Volumes I and II **2nd Impression**)
**DIO CHRYSOSTOM.** <note>A Greek orator and philosopher known for his "Discourses" on kingship, virtue, and morality.</note> 5 Volumes. Volumes I and II. J. W. Cohoon. Volume III. J. W. Cohoon and H. Lamar Crosby. Volumes IV and V. H. Lamar Crosby. (Volumes I-III **2nd Impression**)
**DIODORUS OF SICILY.** <note>original: "DIODORUS SICULUS"; author of a "Universal History" that compiled the history of the world from mythical times to the Roman era.</note> 12 Volumes. Volumes I-V. C. H. Oldfather. Volume IX. Russel M. Geer. (Volumes I-III **2nd Impression**)
**DIOGENES LAERTIUS.** <note>The primary source for the lives and sayings of the ancient Greek philosophers.</note> R. D. Hicks. 2 Volumes. (Volume I **4th Impression**, Volume II **3rd Impression**)
**DIONYSIUS OF HALICARNASSUS: ROMAN ANTIQUITIES.** <note>A history of early Rome written by a Greek teacher to demonstrate to his countrymen that the Romans were of noble, Greek descent.</note> Spelman’s translation revised by E. Cary. 7 Volumes. (Volumes I-IV **2nd Impression**)
**EPICTETUS.** <note>A former slave turned Stoic philosopher who taught that happiness is found in accepting what we cannot change.</note> W. A. Oldfather. 2 Volumes. (Volume I **2nd Impression**)
**EURIPIDES.** <note>One of the three great tragedians of Athens, known for his psychological realism and focus on the inner lives of women and slaves.</note> A. S. Way. 4 Volumes. (Volume I **7th Impression**, Volumes II-IV **6th Impression**) Verse translation.
**EUSEBIUS: ECCLESIASTICAL HISTORY.** <note>The first comprehensive history of the Christian Church from the time of the Apostles to the 4th century.</note> Kirsopp Lake and

# THE LOEB CLASSICAL LIBRARY

[**EUSEBIUS: THE ECCLESIASTICAL HISTORY.** <note>Continued from the previous page; Eusebius was a 4th-century bishop known as the "Father of Church History."</note>] J. E. L. Oulton. 2 Volumes. (Volume I **2nd Impression**, Volume II **3rd Impression**)
**GALEN: ON THE NATURAL FACULTIES.** <note>Galen was a prominent Greek physician and philosopher in the Roman Empire; this work details his theories on how the body’s organs function.</note> A. J. Brock. (**3rd Impression**)
**THE GREEK ANTHOLOGY.** <note>A massive collection of short poems and epigrams spanning the Classical to the Byzantine periods.</note> W. R. Paton. 5 Volumes. (Volumes I and II **4th Impression**, Volumes III and IV **3rd Impression**)
**THE GREEK BUCOLIC POETS (THEOCRITUS, BION, MOSCHUS).** <note>These poets wrote "pastoral" poetry, which idealized the simple lives and songs of shepherds in the countryside.</note> J. M. Edmonds. (**7th Impression revised.**)
**GREEK ELEGY AND IAMBUS WITH THE ANACREONTEA.** <note>A collection of early Greek lyric poetry, including mournful or moralizing "elegies" and satirical "iambic" verse.</note> J. M. Edmonds. 2 Volumes. (Volume I **2nd Impression**)
**GREEK MATHEMATICAL WORKS.** Ivor Thomas. 2 Volumes. (**2nd Impression**)
**HERODES.** <note>A poet known for his short, realistic dramatic scenes called "mimes."</note> *Compare* **THEOPHRASTUS: CHARACTERS.**
**HERODOTUS.** <note>Known as the "Father of History," he wrote about the cultures and wars of the ancient Mediterranean world.</note> A. D. Godley. 4 Volumes. (Volumes I–III **4th Impression**, Volume IV **3rd Impression**)
**HESIOD AND THE HOMERIC HYMNS.** <note>Hesiod was an early epic poet; the "Homeric Hymns" are a collection of poems honoring the various Greek gods.</note> H. G. Evelyn White. (**7th Impression revised and enlarged.**)
**HIPPOCRATES AND THE FRAGMENTS OF HERACLEITUS.** <note>Hippocrates is traditionally the founder of Western medicine, while Heracleitus was a philosopher who taught that change is the fundamental essence of the universe.</note> W. H. S. Jones and E. T. Withington. 4 Volumes. (Volume I **3rd Impression**, Volumes II–IV **2nd Impression**)
**HOMER: ILIAD.** <note>The ancient epic poem recounting the events of the Trojan War.</note> A. T. Murray. 2 Volumes. (**6th Impression**)
**HOMER: ODYSSEY.** <note>The epic sequel to the Iliad, following Odysseus’s ten-year journey home.</note> A. T. Murray. 2 Volumes. (**7th Impression**)
**ISAEUS.** <note>An Athenian orator who specialized in legal cases regarding inheritance.</note> E. S. Forster. (**2nd Impression**)
**ISOCRATES.** <note>An influential Greek rhetorician and teacher who promoted political unity among the Greeks.</note> George Norlin and LaRue Van Hook. 3 Volumes.
**ST. JOHN DAMASCENE: BARLAAM AND IOASAPH.** <note>A Christian adaptation of the story of the Buddha, framed as a tale of conversion in India.</note> Reverend G. R. Woodward and Harold Mattingly. (**2nd Impression revised.**)
**JOSEPHUS.** <note>A 1st-century Jewish historian whose works are essential for understanding the Jewish-Roman wars and the historical context of early Christianity.</note> H. St. J. Thackeray and Ralph Marcus. 9 Volumes. Volumes I–VII. (Volumes I, V and VI **2nd Impression**)
**JULIAN.** <note>The Emperor Julian, often called "the Apostate," who attempted to restore traditional Roman paganism.</note> Wilmer Cave Wright. 3 Volumes. (Volume I **2nd Impression**, Volume II **3rd Impression**)
**LONGUS: DAPHNIS AND CHLOE.** <note>A famous ancient Greek novel about the romance between two young shepherds.</note> Thornley's translation revised by J. M. Edmonds; and **PARTHENIUS.** <note>A compiler of tragic love stories for poets to use as source material.</note> S. Gaselee. (**3rd Impression**)
**LUCIAN.** <note>A witty satirist known for his dialogues poking fun at traditional religion and philosophy.</note> A. M. Harmon. 8 Volumes. Volumes I–V. (Volumes I, II and IV **2nd Impression**, Volume III **3rd Impression**)
**LYCOPHRON.** <note>A Hellenistic poet known for his difficult and cryptic poem, the "Alexandra."</note> *Compare* **CALLIMACHUS.**
**LYRA GRAECA.** <note>A comprehensive collection of Greek lyric poetry fragments.</note> J. M. Edmonds. 3 Volumes. (Volume I **3rd Impression**, Volume II **2nd Edition revised and enlarged**, Volume III **3rd Impression revised.**)
**LYSIAS.** <note>A celebrated Athenian professional speechwriter noted for his clear and pure style.</note> W. R. Lamb. (**2nd Impression**)
**MANETHO.** <note>An Egyptian priest who wrote a history of Egypt in Greek.</note> W. G. Waddell; **PTOLEMY: THE FOUR BOOKS.** <note>original: "TETRABIBLOS"; the foundational text on the principles of astrology by the astronomer Claudius Ptolemy.</note> F. E. Robbins. (**2nd Impression**)
**MARCUS AURELIUS.** <note>The Roman Emperor and Stoic philosopher whose personal journals comprise the "Meditations."</note> C. R. Haines. (**3rd Impression revised.**)

**MENANDER.** <note>Menander was the leading writer of Athenian "New Comedy," focusing on clever plots about family life, love, and misunderstandings rather than politics.</note> F. G. Allinson. (**2nd Impression revised.**)
**MINOR ATTIC ORATORS.** <note>A collection of speeches by lesser-known but historically significant Athenian public speakers, such as Antiphon and Andocides.</note> 2 Volumes. Volume I (Antiphon, Andocides). K. J. Maidment.
**NONNOS: DIONYSIACA.** <note>A massive, elaborate epic poem from the 5th century AD telling the life story of the god Dionysus.</note> W. H. D. Rouse. 3 Volumes. (Volume III **2nd Impression**)
**OPPIAN, COLLUTHUS, TRYPHIODORUS.** <note>A volume of poets from the later Roman era who wrote instructional poems on fishing and hunting, as well as accounts of the Trojan War.</note> A. W. Mair.
**PAPYRI. NON-LITERARY SELECTIONS.** <note>Transcripts of everyday life—contracts, letters, and receipts—recovered from ancient Egyptian trash heaps and burials.</note> A. S. Hunt and C. C. Edgar. 2 Volumes. (Volume I **2nd Impression**) **LITERARY SELECTIONS.** <note>Fragments of lost literature and poetry preserved on papyrus scraps.</note> Volume I (Poetry). D. L. Page. (**3rd Impression**)
**PARTHENIUS.** <note>A Greek poet and grammarian whose mythological stories of tragic love influenced Roman literature.</note> *See* **LONGUS.**
**PAUSANIAS: DESCRIPTION OF GREECE.** <note>A fascinating 2nd-century travelogue that describes the monuments, local myths, and history of mainland Greece.</note> W. H. S. Jones. 5 Volumes and Companion Volume arranged by R. E. Wycherley. (Volumes I and III **2nd Impression**)
**PHILO.** <note>Philo of Alexandria was a Jewish philosopher who sought to harmonize the Torah with Greek philosophy, particularly Platonism.</note> 11 Volumes. Volumes I–V. F. H. Colson and Reverend G. H. Whitaker; Volumes VI–IX. F. H. Colson. (Volumes I, II, V, VI and VII **2nd Impression**, Volume IV **3rd Impression revised.**)
**PHILOSTRATUS: THE LIFE OF APOLLONIUS OF TYANA.** <note>A semi-legendary biography of a 1st-century wandering philosopher and miracle-worker.</note> F. C. Conybeare. 2 Volumes. (**3rd Impression**)
**PHILOSTRATUS: IMAGES; CALLISTRATUS: DESCRIPTIONS.** <note>Works of "ekphrasis," where the authors provide vivid literary descriptions of paintings and sculptures.</note> A. Fairbanks.
**PHILOSTRATUS AND EUNAPIUS: LIVES OF THE SOPHISTS.** <note>Biographies of the great public speakers and teachers of the Roman Imperial period.</note> Wilmer Cave Wright. (**2nd Impression**)
**PINDAR.** <note>Ancient Greece's most famous lyric poet, best known for his "victory odes" celebrating winners of the Olympic and other athletic games.</note> Sir J. E. Sandys. (**7th Impression revised.**)
**PLATO I: EUTHYPHRO, APOLOGY, CRITO, PHAEDO, PHAEDRUS.** <note>Dialogues concerning the trial and execution of Socrates and the nature of the soul.</note> H. N. Fowler. (**9th Impression**)
**PLATO II: THEAETETUS AND SOPHIST.** <note>Advanced philosophical inquiries into the nature of knowledge and the definition of a philosopher.</note> H. N. Fowler. (**4th Impression**)
**PLATO III: STATESMAN, PHILEBUS.** H. N. Fowler; **ION.** W. R. M. Lamb. (**4th Impression**)
**PLATO IV: LACHES, PROTAGORAS, MENO, EUTHYDEMUS.** <note>Dialogues exploring the nature of courage and whether virtue can be taught.</note> W. R. M. Lamb. (**3rd Impression revised.**)
**PLATO V: LYSIS, SYMPOSIUM, GORGIAS.** <note>Famous works regarding friendship, the nature of Love (the Symposium), and the art of persuasion.</note> W. R. M. Lamb. (**4th Impression revised.**)
**PLATO VI: CRATYLUS, PARMENIDES, GREATER HIPPIAS, LESSER HIPPIAS.** <note>Investigates the origins of language and the nature of beauty and truth.</note> H. N. Fowler. (**3rd Impression**)
**PLATO VII: TIMAEUS, CRITIAS, CLITOPHO, MENEXENUS, LETTERS.** <note>original: "EPISTULAE"</note> <note>These works cover Plato's cosmology, the story of Atlantis, and his personal correspondence.</note> Reverend R. G. Bury. (**3rd Impression**)
**PLATO VIII: CHARMIDES, ALCIBIADES, HIPPARCHUS, THE LOVERS, THEAGES, MINOS AND EPINOMIS.** W. R. M. Lamb.
**PLATO: LAWS.** <note>Plato's final and longest dialogue, offering a practical blueprint for the legal system of a city-state.</note> Reverend R. G. Bury. 2 Volumes. (**2nd Impression**)
**PLATO: REPUBLIC.** <note>Plato’s seminal work on justice, the ideal state, and the "philosopher king."</note> Paul Shorey. 2 Volumes. (Volume I **4th Impression**, Volume II **3rd Impression**)

**PLUTARCH: ETHICAL ESSAYS.** <note>original: "Moralia"; a vast collection of 78 essays and transcribed speeches on customs, religion, philosophy, and practical advice for daily life.</note> 14 Volumes. Volumes I–V. F. C. Babbitt; Volume VI. W. C. Helmbold; Volume X. H. N. Fowler. (Volumes I, III and X **2nd Impression**)
**PLUTARCH: THE PARALLEL LIVES.** <note>A series of biographies pairing famous Greeks with famous Romans (such as Alexander the Great and Julius Caesar) to compare their characters and virtues.</note> B. Perrin. 11 Volumes. (**Volumes I, II and VII 3rd Impression, Volumes III, IV, VI, VIII–XI 2nd Impression**)
**POLYBIUS.** <note>A Greek historian of the Hellenistic period, best known for his "Histories," which explain how the Roman Republic rose to dominate the Mediterranean world.</note> W. R. Paton. 6 Volumes.
**PROCOPIUS: HISTORY OF THE WARS.** <note>The principal historian of the 6th century, Procopius recorded the military campaigns of the Emperor Justinian and his general Belisarius.</note> H. B. Dewing. 7 Volumes. (**Volume I 2nd Impression**)
**PTOLEMY: FOUR BOOKS.** <note>original: "Tetrabiblos"; a foundational work on the philosophy and practice of astrology by the famous astronomer and geographer Claudius Ptolemy.</note> *Compare* **MANETHO.**
**QUINTUS SMYRNAEUS.** <note>A Greek epic poet who wrote "The Fall of Troy," filling the chronological gap between Homer’s "Iliad" and "Odyssey."</note> A. S. Way. (**2nd Impression**) Verse translation.
**SEXTUS EMPIRICUS.** <note>A physician and philosopher whose writings are the primary source for Greek Skepticism, a school of thought that advocated for suspending judgment to achieve peace of mind.</note> Rev. R. G. Bury. 4 Volumes. (Volumes I and III **2nd Impression**)
**SOPHOCLES.** <note>One of the three great ancient Greek tragedians; his most famous plays include "Oedipus Rex" and "Antigone."</note> F. Storr. 2 Volumes. (Volume I **9th Impression**, Volume II **6th Impression**) Verse translation.
**STRABO: GEOGRAPHY.** <note>A comprehensive 17-volume encyclopedia of geographical knowledge, including history and folklore, from the era of the Roman Empire.</note> Horace L. Jones. 8 Volumes. (Volumes I and VIII **3rd Impression**, Volumes II, V and VI **2nd Impression**)
**THEOPHRASTUS: CHARACTERS.** <note>A series of short, humorous sketches identifying various types of human personality flaws, like "The Flatterer" or "The Grumbler."</note> J. M. Edmonds; **HERODES**, etc. A. D. Knox. (**2nd Impression**)
**THEOPHRASTUS: ENQUIRY INTO PLANTS.** <note>original: "Historia Plantarum"; one of the most important books of ancient natural science, providing a detailed classification of the plant kingdom.</note> Sir Arthur Hort. 2 Volumes. (**2nd Impression**)
**THUCYDIDES.** <note>An Athenian general and historian who wrote the definitive history of the Peloponnesian War between Athens and Sparta.</note> C. F. Smith. 4 Volumes. (Volume I **3rd Impression**, Volumes II–IV **2nd Impression revised**)
**TRYPHIODORUS.** <note>A 3rd or 4th-century Egyptian Greek poet who wrote a short epic on the "Destruction of Troy."</note> *Compare* **OPPIAN.**
**XENOPHON: THE EDUCATION OF CYRUS.** <note>original: "Cyropaedia"; a partly fictionalized biography of Cyrus the Great, intended to describe the ideal education and character of a ruler.</note> Walter Miller. 2 Volumes. (Volume I **2nd Impression**, Volume II **3rd Impression**)
**XENOPHON: GREEK AFFAIRS, THE MARCH UP-COUNTRY, APOLOGY, AND SYMPOSIUM.** <note>original titles: "Hellenica" (a history of Greece), "Anabasis" (the story of 10,000 Greek mercenaries), "Apology" (Socrates' defense), and "Symposium" (a philosophical dinner party).</note> C. L. Brownson and O. J. Todd. 3 Volumes. (Volumes I and III **3rd Impression**, Volume II **4th Impression**)
**XENOPHON: MEMORABILIA AND THE ESTATE MANAGER.** <note>original: "Memorabilia" (recollections of Socrates) and "Oeconomicus" (a treatise on managing a household and farm).</note> E. C. Marchant. (**2nd Impression**)
**XENOPHON: MINOR WORKS.** <note>original: "Scripta Minora"; a collection of shorter essays on topics such as hunting, horsemanship, and the Spartan constitution.</note> E. C. Marchant. (**2nd Impression**)
